rows.form_notes: proc.cmdline given as bare "bash" rather than the full `bash -lc ...` script text — a granularity compression that is story-grounded and did not drive the verdict
rows.rationale:
The observed payload's single row (2026-07-25T09:29:02.246Z) carries falco.output_fields.evt.type
"openat", while both live controls (C-14d, C-21d) returned row_count 0, so the delta is real and the
projection correctly reproduces falco.rule "Adding ssh keys to authorized_keys", fd.name
"/root/.ssh/authorized_keys", user.name "root", and correctly placeholders the volatile container.id.
However the projection asserts falco.output_fields.evt.type: "write" — a fully concrete value that the
story never states (it says only that "the write is performed by a bash process", never a syscall) and
that the telemetry contradicts, since Falco surfaced the openat that opened authorized_keys. Because the
story does not ground the syscall, the compliant output was a placeholder such as <evt-type>; emitting a
concrete, telemetry-contradicting value is C-FABRICATED-VALUE. The abbreviated cmdline "bash" is
story-grounded granularity loss and is recorded in form_notes only.
rows.evidence: The single query (elastic.falco-alerts) returned row_count 1 in the operation window: a 2026-07-25T09:29:02.246Z alert with falco.rule "Adding ssh keys to authorized_keys", falco.output_fields.fd.name "/root/.ssh/authorized_keys", user.name "root", evt.type "openat", and a proc.cmdline appending "ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAAD_fake_key_0_${ts}_attacker attacker@elsewhere" to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys. Two of the three controls are live (C-14d 2026-07-11 and C-21d 2026-07-04, both window_live: true) and each returned row_count 0 with values: []; only C-7d is dead and is disregarded. The distinction is carried by non-volatile surfaced fields — falco.output_fields.fd.name, user.name and proc.cmdline — not by the unstable falco.output_fields.container.id (1df4bcd65ee4), so the delta survives the environment's unstable-identifier caveat. No truncation flags are set on any payload.

The `baseline` is empty because, per `environment_notes.state_and_lookup_systems`, cmdb queries have no `@timestamp` bounds to move and therefore no baseline-diff semantics, matching the measurement's `state-only` reading. The story's activity is a single local append to `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` on canary-1, which changes no CMDB entity record, so there is no delta for this lead to represent. The empty projection asserts no change and fabricates no concrete CMDB fields (e.g. no invented owner or criticality), which is the faithful response to a state-only envelope.
